title: Sable and the Salt
premise: Juniper Ashgrove has spent her life carving bones into instruments of memory, keeping the Salt Guild's ledgers while pretending she cannot hear the dead whisper through her work. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, she learns the covenant binding the mortal realm to the Sable Court was sealed with a name—hers, given before she was born—and its breach is unraveling both worlds. To reforge it she must cross into the Sable realm with Kestrel Vane, the guild's disgraced enforcer who once loved her and betrayed her, trading pieces of her own remembered life as toll for each ward she restores. In the end Juniper must choose between reclaiming her stolen identity or surrendering it to become the living covenant itself; she chooses a third path, splitting the covenant between herself and Kestrel, binding them together across realms as the stars reignite.
about_author: A. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in coastal museum basements. They write fantasy about grief, trade, and the things people bury on purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A night of routine work at the Salt Guild: cataloguing a bone flute that plays a dead woman's lullaby, hiding her gift from her superiors. The dead murmur warnings she pretends not to hear. Emotional beat: the loneliness of deliberate invisibility, and the first crack in it when a carved rib whispers her true name.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The border wards fail at moonrise; every star vanishes simultaneously, and the guild hall floods with ghosts demanding payment of an old debt. Kestrel Vane returns after seven years' exile, carrying a shard of fallen wardstone that hums when Juniper touches it. Emotional beat: terror braided with recognition—the past walking back through the door.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He reveals the covenant was signed generations ago with an Ashgrove name, and the guild erased Juniper's origins to keep her compliant. Confronted by Master Aldous, who wants Juniper sacrificed to buy time, they flee together. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal—by institution, by history, and by the man who knew first.

chapters.title: Tollgate of Small Memories
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the first broken ward, the crossing demands payment: Juniper surrenders the memory of her mother's face to seal it. She and Kestrel begin the road into Sable country, old wounds reopening in conversation. Emotional beat: grief as currency, and the terrible intimacy of traveling with someone you once loved.

chapters.title: The Drowned Market
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In a Sable border town where goods are traded for hours of life, they seek a guide and find instead the ghost of Juniper's grandmother, who explains the covenant's original terms. Sable agents shadow them. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Juniper realizes how much of her life has been pre-spent.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Debt
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ambushed by the Sable Court's huntsmen, Kestrel bargains with his own remaining years to save Juniper, confessing that his exile was punishment for refusing to deliver her as a child. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud, and Juniper's fury that becomes something closer to forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Court of Unlit Candles
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They reach the Sable Court, starless and beautiful, where the Queen of Ash offers Juniper restoration of everything she's paid—if she takes the covenant alone and forgets Kestrel entirely. Emotional beat: temptation at full strength; love tested against the longing to be whole.

chapters.title: Bone-Carver's Choice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climax begins: Juniper refuses the Queen's bargain and instead carves a new covenant-bone from the wardstone shard and her own forearm bone, a working no one has survived. The Court erupts; Kestrel fights free of the guards to reach her. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not recovered—she defines what her name means.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Covenant
chapters.summary: Climax. Juniper and Kestrel bind themselves jointly to the covenant, splitting its weight so neither is consumed; the ritual nearly kills them both. The stars reignite one constellation at a time as the wards rebuild along their shared bond. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into partnership; the cost made bearable because it is shared.

chapters.title: Sable and the Salt
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. Months later: Juniper runs a reformed guild that trades honestly with the Sable realm, hearing the dead without shame, missing some memories but writing new ones. Kestrel, half-bound to the other side, visits through the restored wards. Emotional beat: quiet peace—not restoration, but something better built in its place.
